thread:
sam: Heads up — AlertManager fired for a big auth-backoff spike, started ~06:02 UTC. Lots of token_refresh_backoff logs and a cascade of session revokes.

incidents-bot: [ALERT] auth-backoff-surge (sev=2) — 320 events in 5m, spike in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Link: https://internal/alerts/AB-4821 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm seeing hundreds of `429` from our auth proxy plus a surge of `session.revoke` events from the session service. Any config changes in the last 12h?

aya: Not from infra side. But ops rolled the new RBAC sync at 02:10 UTC that forces TTL refresh for service tokens — could be related.

jordan: Logs show many users hitting refresh loops after the RBAC sync invalidated some cached roles. Example log snippet:```
ERROR auth: token_refresh_backoff user=alice@example.com attempts=7 backoff_ms=32000 region=us-east-1 svc=session
WARN rbac: cache_miss key=user:alice roles=none source=rbac-sync
INFO session: revoke user=alice@example.com reason=role-mismatch request_id=01F...
```

sam: That matches. RBAC sync triggered role mismatches -> session revokes -> clients try refresh -> backoff -> repeat. MFA push noise also reported in support queue (MFA fatigue).

maria: Support pinged — some enterprise tenants saw mass prompts. We should contain: 1) throttle session.revoke fanout 2) pause RBAC sync rollout 3) temporary allowlist for session refresh for affected tenants.

aya: I'll pause the RBAC sync rollout now. Command:```
kubectl -n infra rollout pause deployment/rbac-sync-v2
```

incidents-bot: Action recorded by aya at 06:05 UTC — rollout paused.

jordan: For immediate mitigation I pushed a short-term change to session service to convert `revoke -> soft_revoke` for users with more than X active sessions to avoid cascade. Patch applied:```
PATCH /internal/session-config
{ "revoke_mode": "soft_when_bulk" }
```

sam: Nice. Also rate-limited token refresh endpoint to 200rps per tenant and enabled jitter on refresh to break thundering herds.

maria: After these changes, error rate dropped ~80% within 3m. Support reports MFA prompts falling.

secops: We need to run a short blast radius audit: list tenants with >=50 revoke events between 06:00-06:10, collect session IDs, and notify SOC for suspicious pattern detection. I'll pull from audit log.

jordan: I exported the affected sessions to S3: s3://redwood-incident-exports/2061212121/rbac-backoff-surge.csv (access restricted). Included fields: user_email, session_id, revoke_reason, timestamp, region.

aya: Post-incident actions I'm proposing: 1) Rollback RBAC sync to v1; 2) Add preflight check in RBAC rollout to detect large cache misses; 3) Add exponential jitter on our SDK refresh logic; 4) Create runbook entry for auth-backoff scenarios.

maria: Also add a flag to avoid synchronous global session.revoke fanout — make it incremental by tenant.

sam: Agreed. Who wants the postmortem? I'll own timeline + mitigation steps. Jordan take logs/export and craft detection queries for future alerting. Aya and Maria own deployment guardrails. Secops own tenant notifications and SOC runbook.

secops: We'll notify affected customers via the incident template and offer guidance for SDK versions that do refresh with backoff. Draft message ready in #customer-commms.

jordan: One more note — KMS rotation was scheduled for 03:00 UTC but completed earlier, any chance that overlapped? I checked, KMS ops shows rotation at 03:01 and no errors. Not related.

maria: Good to confirm. Let's keep this thread for any follow-ups. I'll open a postmortem doc and link in here.

sam: TL;DR: RBAC sync invalidated caches -> mass session revokes -> client refresh storms -> token backoff -> MFA fatigue. Contained via pause, soft_revokes, rate-limits, jitter. Postmortem + runbooks assigned. :white_check_mark:
